recon.summary: Perform reconnaissance on targets (ip, url, emails, usernames, etc.).
recon.details:
Performs reconnaissance across a variety of target identifiers such as IPs, URLs, emails, and usernames.
Supports multi-target scanning, parallel/background execution, and conditional logic through operators.
Typical workflow: recon → find_exploit → exploit → clean_up.
Results can be piped or linked into subsequent commands for automated chaining.

find_exploit.summary: Search exploit databases for vulnerabilities matching discovered targets.
find_exploit.details:
Finds and maps known exploits against data gathered from the reconnaissance phase.
Searches both local and remote databases, including exploit-db and user-defined sources.
Filters can be applied using target_id, vulnerability name, or risk level.
Outputs can be linked directly into the 'exploit' phase for automation.

db.description: Exploit database to query (exploit-db, local, or custom)

limit.description: Limit the number of results returned

exploit.summary: Attempt an exploit against a target using a selected payload or module.
exploit.details:
Executes exploit modules against a specified target based on data gathered from previous phases.
Can operate in safe (simulation) or unsafe (live) mode.
Supports credential-based logins, timeout configurations, and post-exploit session management.
Commonly linked from 'find_exploit' to automate exploitation chains.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds for exploit attempt

dry_run.description: Validate the exploit without performing destructive actions

clean_up.summary: Clean up after exploitation, removing artifacts or reverting changes.
clean_up.details:
Runs post-operation cleanup tasks to remove exploit artifacts, temporary files, or system changes.
Optionally preserves logs for review or reporting.
Can be executed manually or automatically at the end of a workflow.

parallel.summary: Run grouped commands concurrently within a single workflow.
parallel.details:
Executes multiple commands simultaneously with optional concurrency control.
Useful for parallel scanning, exploit testing, or distributed tasks.
Can automatically aggregate results upon completion.

commands.description: List of commands to run concurrently

summary_on_complete.description: Show a summary once all tasks finish

gates.summary: Evaluate conditional expressions for branching workflows.
gates.details:
Acts as the logical controller of your workflow chain.
Evaluates conditional expressions and determines which branches to execute based on global or local variables.
Typically represented by operators such as 'if(...) { } else { }'.

expression.description: Conditional expression referencing globals and outputs

globals.description: Global modifiers referenced/modified by the expression

run.summary: Execute the currently selected or active .bline module.
run.details:
Runs the current configuration or active .bline chain immediately.
Acts as a one-shot trigger and respects all previously loaded parameters or linked configurations.
No arguments are required.

use.summary: Temporarily load one or more .bline modules for immediate use.
use.details:
Allows quick activation of modules for on-the-fly use.
Accepts either file paths or numeric indexes generated from 'list' output.
Modules remain active until explicitly replaced or reset.

path_or_index.description: One or more paths or indices to load

import.summary: Import an external .bline file into the local workspace database.
import.details:
Adds an existing .bline module from disk into the persistent local database.
Once imported, modules become accessible via the 'list' and 'use' commands.

path.description: Path to the .bline file to import

overwrite.description: Overwrite if the file already exists in DB

export.summary: Export a stored .bline file to a chosen location.
export.details:
Writes a .bline module from the local database to disk for sharing or backup.
If no path is provided, exports to the user's home directory by default.

edit.summary: Open and edit a .bline module in the configured editor.
edit.details:
Launches either an inline editor or an external editor (based on configuration) to modify a .bline file.
If the specified file does not exist, the system will prompt to create it.

id_or_path.description: ID or file path to edit

delete.summary: Delete a .bline file from disk or the workspace database.
delete.details:
Removes a .bline module from the system.
Supports both file paths and database references.
When 'force' is false, user confirmation is required before deletion.

id_or_path.description: ID or path of the .bline to delete
